Asha M.: Heads-up: ACME pilot shows churn signals. want a short, copy-paste runbook the SE can send to their eng lead. focus: prefills, streaming fallback, quick metrics to paste in a support ticket.
Duncan B.: I can do a compact one-pager. keep it action-first, no more than 6 bullets.
Lena S.: include a tiny SDK snippet for exponential backoff + stream->poll transition. many customers love copy/paste.
Marco P.: add exactly which metrics to capture and the minimal thresholds that mean we should intervene. also suggest a light-cost prefll model (if they have mixed tiers).
onboard-bot: New draft created: https://console.redwood.ai/templates/midpilot-stabilizer (internal) :memo:

Duncan B.: DRAFT RUNBOOK: "Mid-pilot Stabilizer (customer-facing)"
- Quick context: Designed for mid-market pilots where ticket volume is rising and renewals are under discussion. Follow these steps before escalating.

1) Fast sanity (1-2 min)
   - Confirm model + variant pinned (avoid unexpected autoswitch): `GET /v1/tenants/<TID>` check `model` and `variant`
   - Confirm streaming endpoint reachable: open WS/SSE and expect first bytes < 500ms.

2) Lightweight prefill (ops-friendly)
   - Purpose: populate prefix KV and warm worker pools. Send short deterministic prompts 3-10 minutes before expected traffic burst. Keep each prompt <= 16 tokens.
   - Suggested pattern: 20 short requests spaced over ~3 minutes. Use a cheaper variant (e.g., small/low-cost) if available.

3) Safe client defaults (copy/paste)
   - Prefer micro-batches; set small concurrency and short throttle. Example SDK settings: 
```js
// pseudocode
client.defaults = {
  batchWindowMs: 40,
  maxConcurrency: 6,
  streamStallMs: 1200,
  resumeMaxTokens: 48
}
```

4) Stream -> poll fallback (minimal effort)
   - If no token emitted for > 1200ms: try a `resume` request (max_tokens=32). If still none after 2 tries, switch to polling every 250ms until completion. Log `stream_fallback` and the last received offset.

5) Minimal metrics to capture (paste into support)
   - active_sessions (5m avg), avg_token_latency_ms (5m), prefix_cache_hit_rate (5m), error_rate_percent (5m).
   - Quick thresholds to triage: avg_token_latency_ms > 200 → investigate batching/prefill; prefix_cache_hit_rate < 45% → increase warmup; error_rate_percent > 1.5% or any 5xx spikes → escalate.

6) Quick escalation payload (copy/paste into support chat)
   - tenant: <TENANT_ID>
   - sample_request: <REQUEST_ID>
   - symptom: slow tokens / stream stalls / higher-than-expected cost
   - metrics snapshot (paste JSON from step 7)

7) One-command metrics dump (customer with API key)
```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  "https://metrics.redwood.ai/tenants/<TENANT_ID>/window?m=active_sessions,avg_token_latency_ms,prefix_cache_hit_rate,error_rate_percent&window=5m"
```

8) Low-friction customer note (email/SE message)
   - "Hi — we saw intermittent token lag during your pilot. Quick fixes: enable a short prefill (few mins), use the stream->poll fallback, and set micro-batching. If you can paste the metrics dump from the curl above, we’ll review within 1 business hour."

Lena S.: nice. add a short retry/backoff snippet customers can use for polling so they don't overload.

Duncan B.: Added small backoff pattern: poll 4x at 250ms, then 3x at 500ms, then stop and surface to UI.

Marco P.: For internal ops: if customer metrics show avg_token_latency_ms > 220 AND prefix_cache_hit_rate < 40 for 10m, flag as LEVEL-2 and page SRE. Also note if `x-rd-fallback-model` header appears repeatedly, that means dedicated pool hit an overflow and CS should propose dedicated bump or scheduled warm windows.

Asha M.: Perfect. Can we make the runbook a PDF for customer handoff + 2-line internal triage note? I'll own the outreach.

onboard-bot: Runbook saved to /docs/onboarding/customer-facing/midpilot-stabilizer-v1 and internal triage note created. :white_check_mark:

Marco P.: leaving a tiny UX tip — recommend showing a subtle progress indicator when client does resume/poll fallback so end-users don't think the chat died. small wins on perceived reliability. :sparkles:

Duncan B.: will finalize and attach the PDF in the enablement space. tagging @Asha to review customer tone.

Asha M.: will review and send. thanks everyone. :raised_hands:
